title: Optimizing parameters for multiband ABRs to continuous speech

description: This dataset comprises multiband auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) recorded from 40 participants (15 in Experiment 1, 25 in Experiment 2) listening to continuous peaky speech stimuli. Experiment 1 investigates the effect of chirp-phase versus zero-phase profiles on ABR amplitudes, while Experiment 2 examines the influence of fundamental frequency (f0) across different narrators. The dataset includes raw EEG recordings in Brain Products format, stimulus files with audio and deconvolution regressors, and comprehensive event metadata, designed to optimize parameters for measuring frequency-specific ABRs to naturalistic speech.
methods_description: EEG recordings were collected from participants seated in a sound-isolating booth while passively listening to audiobook stimuli presented at 65 dB SPL through ER-2 insert earphones at 48 kHz sampling rate. Experiment 1 (October-December 2022) presented 720 trials (120 minutes total) of multiband peaky speech with zero- or chirp-phase profiles. Experiment 2 (January-April 2023) presented 840 trials (140 minutes total) of multiband peaky speech from two narrators at natural and shifted fundamental frequencies (100 Hz). Stimulus presentation and experiment control were managed using custom Python scripts with expyfun. Raw EEG data were recorded in Brain Products format (.eeg, .vhdr, .vmrk files), with stimuli and regressors stored in HDF5 format.
